title: Photosynthesis and Respiration
seo_title: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Photosynthesis and Respiration Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Photosynthesis and respiration
standard_text: Photosynthesis: plants use light energy, water and carbon dioxide to make glucose and oxygen, in chloroplasts. Respiration: all living cells release energy from glucose using oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water. The two processes balance gases in the atmosphere. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 8, Life and Living: Photosynthesis and respiration)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the word equations for photosynthesis and respiration, factors that affect photosynthesis, and the starch test. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Photosynthesis stores energy; respiration releases it.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts. Plants store glucose as starch; iodine solution turns blue-black when starch is present.

Respiration happens in every living cell, day and night: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy. Without enough oxygen, cells use anaerobic respiration (fermentation), which releases less energy.

Example

Which gas is a product of photosynthesis?

We breathe it in.

Answer: oxygen

Example

Do plants respire at night?

Every living cell respires.

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants only photosynthesise and do not respire.
  • Thinking respiration is the same as breathing.
  • Forgetting that light is needed for photosynthesis.

items.q: Nomsa covers half of a leaf with foil for two days, then tests the leaf for starch with iodine. Only the uncovered half turns dark blue-black. What does this show?
c: Leaves make food in the dark.
Light is needed to make food (sugar and starch).
items.e: No light, no photosynthesis.

items.q: Sarah keeps one bean plant in a dark closet for 10 days and one in a sunny window. The closet plant turns yellow and weak. Why?
c: It could not do photosynthesis, so it could not make enough food.
items.e: Plants need light energy to make sugar.

items.q: Why is photosynthesis important for animals and people?

items.e: Life depends on it.

items.q: What food does a plant make during photosynthesis?
items.e: Plants make sugar. Some of it is stored as starch.

items.q: Elna asks where oxygen fits in photosynthesis. Which is true?
c: It stores energy and is used as food and building material.
It comes from the air and enters through tiny openings in leaves (stomata).
It comes from the soil through the roots.
It is released into the air through the leaves.
items.e: Oxygen is released into the air through the leaves.

items.q: Nadia lists the parts of photosynthesis. Is glucose (sugar) an input or an output?
items.e: Glucose (sugar) stores energy and is used as food and building material.

items.q: Which of these does a plant need to make food?
items.e: A plant needs light, water, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll to make food. It does not need oxygen to make food.
